points.t: A soft, painless, mobile, slowly growing lump on the trunk, neck or limbs.
Benign overgrowth of mature fat cells; angiolipomas are tender; Dercum’s disease gives many painful lipomas.
Reassure if small and typical; ultrasound or refer if uncertain; excision only for symptoms or diagnosis.
Soft-tissue sarcoma: larger than 5 cm, deep to fascia, growing, painful or recurrent.

points: Soft, rubbery, mobile, lobulated subcutaneous mass with normal overlying skin. Trunk, shoulders, neck and arms. Painless (except angiolipoma or Dercum).

items.t: Lump that is increasing in size or larger than 5 cm, deep or painful: **urgent direct-access ultrasound** (within 2 weeks) or a suspected sarcoma pathway (NICE NG12).

pearls.t: "Is it bigger than a golf ball, growing, deep or painful?" Then it needs a scan.
Angiolipoma tenderness is common and benign, but multiple painful lumps plus systemic symptoms should prompt thinking of Dercum.
